top.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
top.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. top.title: Caitlin Clark Makes History With Major New Deal As WNBA Star Becomes First-Ever Face Of Two Retail Giants
top.description: Caitlin Clark has made history once again, this time away from the basketball court, after signing a groundbreaking multiyear partnership with DICK’S Sporting Goods and Foot Locker. The Indiana Fever superstar is officially the first athlete to become a brand partner for either retailer, marking another major milestone in her rapidly expanding business career. The exclusive agreement will see Clark appear in national and international campaigns, promote her signature footwear, and participate in fan events across both brands. For the 24-year-old WNBA star, the partnership is particularly meaningful because DICK’S was one of her favorite places to shop growing up. According to the official company announcement , the exclusive multiyear deal will bring Clark’s brand to customers across the United States and internationally. The agreement includes national and global advertising campaigns, promotions for her signature footwear and apparel, in-store experiences, appearances, and community events. Although both retailers have previously collaborated with professional athletes, neither had signed an individual athlete as an official brand partner. The financial terms of Clark’s agreement have not been publicly disclosed. The partnership also marks an important development for DICK’S, which now owns Foot Locker and can promote Clark across both retail networks. top.title: Warriors' Steph Curry conquers old friend Klay Thompson in more ways than one
top.description: Miami's Klay Thompson defends against a shot by Warriors guard Stephen Curry in the first half of Thursday's game at Chase Center. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) Klay Thompson chatted amiably with a handful of familiar reporters before Thursday night's game at Chase Center. He was relaxed and engaged, savoring this week's return to California - two games in Los Angeles, where he spent his high school years, and one in the Bay Area, where he spent his championship years (and then another game Sunday in Sacramento). Thompson marveled at the crisp November sunshine in his former home. He longed for a boat ride on the bay but settled for breakfast at Montclair Egg Shop, a regular stop in his Oakland days. As he stood up and headed out for warmups, Thompson shared one source of frustration - his alma mater, Washington State, lost its season opener Monday night. Davidson rolled to a 76-61 road win, which meant Thompson owed his longtime Splash Brother some cash. Stephen Curry happily collected. "We got the dub," Curry, smiling, said postgame, "so there was healthy monetary value to that." The sight of Curry and Thompson on opposite sides of an NBA game is no longer a novelty, given Thompson's two seasons in Dallas. But it still looks striking, strange, surreal. They spent long stretches defending each other Thursday night, as Curry and the Golden State Warriors pulled away for a 120-100 victory over Thompson and Miami. Curry scored 29 points, defying age once again, while Thompson (11 points) cooled off after scorching shooting in his three previous games. Each player had his moments against the other, most memorably on a third-quarter play when Thompson unleashed a shot fake, watched Curry fly past and then smoothly buried a 3-point shot. In the end, Curry and the Warriors prevailed. And so Thompson sat at his locker postgame, now with a larger group of reporters around him, and marveled at his 38-year-old, former backcourt partner. "It was really fun," Thompson, 36, said of dueling with Curry. "Steph's super crafty, still to this day. It felt good to block his shot, and he made a great up-and-under on me. He had an incredible night. What Steph's doing, I might not have appreciated as much as his teammate because I saw it every night so it became normal. "But to see it as an opponent it's incredible, especially that he's nearing 40. And he moves like a young athlete. All the respect in the world for him. He deserves all the accolades, the adulation, the money. He's just one of one, and the game is going to miss him when he does hang it up." Curry is showing few signs of slowing down, as Thompson suggested. Thursday night's first half was uncommonly quiet, as Curry scored only seven points on 2-for-10 shooting from the field (including 1-for-5 from long distance). top.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
top.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. top.title: Diamonds are forever - phoenix club seek FA Cup upset
top.description: Billy Sharp has come out of retirement to play for AFC Rushden & Diamonds - and is seeking a landmark goal [BBC] The notion of your football club ceasing to exist is unthinkable for many fans, but for supporters of Rushden & Diamonds it became a sad reality in 2011. The Northamptonshire-based side, backed by the late Max Griggs, rocketed through non-league in the 1990s and in 2003 reached the third tier of English football before financial issues after he stepped away ultimately saw them fold. A community lost its focal point, and within years their Nene Park stadium had been razed to the ground. "It was heartbreaking - we knew we'd been robbed." reflected Rob Usher, the chairman of phoenix side AFC Rushden & Diamonds, who will make their FA Cup first-round debut this weekend. "I think it was that anger that probably fuelled the fans saying 'no, we don't accept it. We're not gone, we're not done and we want our club back." 'This is community' Some 2,000 travelling fans will make their way to see the now eighth-tier Diamonds take on League One side Burton Albion on Saturday - a bittersweet reminder of days the supporters of the original club could have once taken for granted. Usher, like many of those involved with the Northern Premier League Division One Midlands side, has followed both incarnations of the club - firstly as a fan, but also as a groundsman and turnstile operator before becoming chairman in 2022. "My first game was an FA Cup tie against Shrewsbury Town in 1998. It was the year we ended up playing Leeds United in the third round." he said. "Rushden & Diamonds gave us some great times. Winning leagues, the Duane Darby's, the Onandi Lowe's of our past. But I tell everyone I've never traded for what we have with AFC Rushden & Diamonds. "This is a community, this is an army of people who turn up and give their time and their money, their care, their devotion... not because they want the club to exist, but because they want the club to thrive. That's why it's so special". Diamonds chairman Rob Usher said the club was at the heart of its community [James Burridge/BBC] Diamonds, who now play their home games at Hayden Road, started their journey to the first round proper with a 5-0 win at Kimberley Miners Welfare in the extra preliminary round on 8 August. They have also beaten Long Eaton United, Desborough Town, Peterborough Sports, Braintree Town and Morecambe to reach this stage. Along with Stafford Rangers, who host Grimsby Town on Sunday, they are the only side left in the competition to have played from the earliest round and have so far earned £23,194 from the FA's prize fund. The winners of the tie at Burton's Pirelli Stadium will collect £47,750, with the losers taking £15,800. All it takes is one team to believe in a quarterback for that quarterback to come off the board early, and Mensah's production has been so dominant that it wouldn't be surprising to see him land near the top of the first round. His arm strength isn't a true weakness, but it doesn't jump off the page like it does for many premier NFL quarterback prospects who are jumping into a league that plays faster all-around. Mensah's ball placement has easily made up for solid but unspectacular arm strength at the college level, but NFL teams will have to evaluate whether they believe that will stand up at the next level. The inconsistent evaluations of Mensah might also be related to Miami's schedule this season. The Hurricanes simply haven't faced many high-level defenses, making it tougher to evaluate his decision-making. That is set to change, of course, as Miami will face Notre Dame and should be in line for at least one big-time matchup in the College Football Playoff. top.title: Virgil van Dijk admits Liverpool's defensive struggles are 'not sustainable'
top.description: Virgil van Dijk admits Liverpool's defensive struggles are 'not sustainable' Virgil van Dijk has warned that Liverpool 's defensive record is 'not sustainable' after Fenerbahce scored three times from set-pieces to beat the Reds 3-2 in Istanbul. Andoni Iraola's side led twice in the Champions League on Wednesday, through Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak, but were pegged back quickly on both occasions before Vedat Muriqi headed a 79th-minute winner. The defeat ended Liverpool's perfect record in this season's league phase, but the worry runs deeper than one result. The Reds had also let in three goals in their wins over Villarreal and LASK, the first time Liverpool have ever conceded three or more in three consecutive major European games. It also means back-to-back defeats for the first time under Iraola, following the loss to Arsenal at the weekend. Liverpool's league record makes for better reading, with only three teams having conceded fewer than their nine goals. However, Van Dijk warned his team that their concession of soft goals cannot continue in Europe. "It's definitely not sustainable. That's why it's a very disappointing night for many reasons, but definitely because of the goals we conceded and the manner we conceded them as well. There is work to do." - Virgil van Dijk The captain singled out the set-piece goals as the most frustrating part of the night. "Three set-pieces as well. We have been very good at them so far this season, but we switched off and weren't ready for the first and second balls. It's a tough one to take," he said. Liverpool face Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, the last game before the international break. They sit fifth with 15 points from nine games. Van Dijk said the clash with the Eagles is 'massive' after successive setbacks for Iraola's side. "It's massive. When we are back in Liverpool, preparing and recovering physically and mentally, we will be looking forward. It is always tough at Palace and I don't expect anything different." 'We cannot lose in the manner we did' The Dutchman believes the setbacks can still strengthen the squad. "I mentioned after the last game [against Arsenal] that we as a group have to go through good moments but also lesser good moments," he said. "That will only form a bigger bond and it will be only beneficial. No-one wants to lose games, especially how we did, but it should only help us in the near future. We should not accept losing, especially in the manner we did."

Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors have flipped the script on their season, and the superstar guard revealed that a message from head coach Steve Kerr after an 0-3 start helped spark the turnaround. Speaking after Thursday’s 120-100 win over the Miami Heat , which extended Golden State’s winning streak to six games, Curry looked back at what Kerr told the team after a loss to the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 24. “It was in Phoenix, I think he was talking about after that game, I know a lot of guys didn’t play, but he just mentioned sticking with the process and the things that he’d noticed on film and just the feel in games, like we were really close to being able to put together, you know, winning performances,” Curry said after the game. Nine Warriors finished with at least eight points, a sign of the depth Kerr has been able to lean on. top.title: Former Australia star Chris Lynn serves one-month ban after testing positive for cocaine on T20 Blast finals day
top.description: Northamptonshire Steelbacks batter Chris Lynn was handed, and served, a one month ban following a positive drug test for cocaine after the club won the T20 Vitality Blast final on July 18th. The Cricket Regulator confirmed that Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) following a drug test taken on Finals Day and an investigation was launched. Lynn’s urine sample was sent to the WADA -accredited Laboratory in the Laboratoire Anti-Dopage, France for analysis and returned Adverse Analytical Findings (“AAF”) for cocaine’s Metabolite benzoylecgonine meaning that it was a violation of cricket’s anti-doping rule. Cocaine is a substance banned “In Competition” but the investigation found that Lynn had taken the drug on the night of July 15th into the early hours of July 16th outside of competition. Northamptonshire won their Blast quarter-final against Gloucestershire that evening. Having also provided evidence supporting this position the regulator accepted that Lynn’s use of cocaine amounted to an out-of-competition ADR violation and was unrelated to sporting performance. The regulator charged Lynn with two ADR violations in September and sought a suspension of three months. The second of those violations – ADR Article 2.2 – in that the Cricketer Used a Prohibited Substance, namely cocaine, on or before 18 July 2026 (the “ADRVs”) – was withdrawn as the reported level of cocaine in the sample was below the minimum reporting level required. Lynn acknowledged and accepted the findings of the regulator and informed them of his decision to undergo a substance of abuse treatment programme. In October, the regulator received evidence that Lynn had completed the programme and his suspension was reduced to one month. That ban was served between Lynn’s provisional suspension on 31 July 2026 until 11.59pm on 30 August 2026. Northants beat Hampshire in the Vitality Blast T20 final at Edgbaston this year (PA) The findings also concluded that there was no requirement to inflict any sanction Northamptonshire Steelbacks. A statement from the Cricket Regulator reads: “The Cricket Regulator has imposed a one-month suspension on former Northamptonshire Steelbacks cricketer Chris Lynn. The period of suspension has now been served. “Mr Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) for the presence of cocaine's Metabolite, benzoylecgonine, related to an In Competition sample collected on the 18 July 2026. “Mr Lynn has accepted the sanction. No further comment will be made on this matter.”

nigeria.title: US federal judge blocks Trump’s massive arch project
nigeria.description: A US federal judge blocked President Donald Trump’s massive triumphal arch project on Thursday, casting doubt over the future of the project hours after it was green-lit by a public commission. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, who is overseeing the case, ruled that the Trump administration cannot start construction on the arch for two weeks while the court considers challenges to its legality. The National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) had voted 8-4 to approve the project earlier Thursday, despite hearing hours of testimony from dozens of furious opponents who questioned its legality and purpose. Chief among the complaints was the location of the 250-foot (76-meter) tall structure: adjacent to the hallowed Arlington National Cemetery, the final resting place for hundreds of thousands of American service members. The giant arch would be much taller than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, its inspiration. It would also tower over the Lincoln Memorial, directly across the Potomac River. The four dissenting commissioners had called for the decision to be delayed, noting there were legal concerns, a lack of congressional appropriation to fund the project and questions about Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s claims of the arch’s military use. But the majority on the panel, which is controlled by Trump allies, voted against a delay and the Trump administration said it aimed to start work right away. Chutkan’s ruling sided with several veterans and the attorneys general of Washington and Virginia, who had sued seeking to halt construction of the arch. – ‘Illegal project’ – The arch is one of several projects launched by Trump in a bid to put his personal stamp on the capital, many of which have prompted legal challenges. They include a White House ballroom, for which Trump had an entire wing of the presidential mansion demolished. The Supreme Court ultimately ruled that the plaintiff who filed suit to halt the project did not have standing. Another is the repeated renovation of the Reflecting Pool, a massive rectangular water basin on the National Mall. Trump has also proposed revamping the East Potomac Golf Links, a historic waterfront Washington golf course, cutting down hundreds of trees before a judge halted the project. The location, a traffic circle currently covered in grass, is key to the Trump administration’s defense of the project. Proponents claim that Congress approved the construction of a monument at the site over a century ago. More than 100 people, often speaking as representatives of organizations, expressed their nearly unanimous opposition. nigeria.title: 14-year-old girl shot as gunmen attack farmers in Nasarawa
nigeria.description: A 14-year-old girl, identified as Amina Ya’u, has sustained gunshot injuries after suspected armed herders opened fire on farmers in Majelisa village, a community bordering Nasarawa and Plateau states. The incident reportedly occurred at about 6:30am on November 5 following reports of sporadic gunshots in the community. Security sources disclosed the development to Zagazola Makama, a counter-insurgency publication, saying troops of Sector 9, Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), deployed at Jenta, immediately responded to a distress call and moved to the scene. According to the report, the troops found the teenage girl with gunshot wounds, while the suspected attackers had fled before their arrival. “Preliminary investigations indicated that a group of armed herders allegedly opened fire on farmers following a disagreement over grazing activities,” the report stated. The troops subsequently evacuated the injured girl to the General Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, for medical attention. Zagazola Makama said engagements with Fulani leaders were ongoing to assist security operatives in identifying and locating the fleeing suspects. It added that troops had intensified patrols and increased their security presence in the area to prevent further violence and possible escalation of the dispute. The incident adds to a series of attacks reported in Nigeria’s North-Central region in recent months. For decades, clashes involving herders and farming communities in the region have resulted in deaths, destruction of farmlands and loss of cattle, amid persistent disputes over land use and grazing activities. nigeria.title: Trump bars future presidents from altering Oval Office
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump has signed an order designating the Oval Office as a national monument, a move he said would prevent future presidents from altering or demolishing the historic space. Trump signed the order on Thursday, extending his focus on White House renovations despite a major midterm election defeat suffered by his Republican Party. Critics have accused the president of paying more attention to construction and renovation projects in Washington than to voters’ concerns over the war in Iran and the rising cost of living, issues that featured prominently ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections. A day after Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump largely ignored the electoral outcome and instead showcased construction work on a new White House ballroom. On Thursday, his attention shifted to the Oval Office, which he has decorated with gold ornaments since returning to power last year, as well as the adjoining Cabinet Room. Trump said the proclamation was intended to protect the two rooms from future alterations. “It won’t be able to be taken down, destroyed, touched, or anything else. It’s called actually a national monument,” he told reporters. The president said the order would make it impossible for future occupants of the White House to carry out building work on the two rooms. The move, however, has fuelled speculation that Trump could be considering further changes to the West Wing, following earlier suggestions that he might relocate reporters from the White House briefing room, which is close to the Oval Office. Trump’s signing of the order was not broadcast by major US television networks. The White House has excluded CNN from the rotating pool of television outlets covering presidential events. The president, however, made a reference to the midterm elections, placing a red baseball cap bearing the word “veto” on the Resolute Desk in front of him. Trump, 80, has threatened to use his presidential powers to block Democratic-backed legislation, although he has also said he is willing to work with the opposition party. nigeria.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ set for blockbuster return after 13 years
nigeria.description: Fans of the violent “Grand Theft Auto” video game franchise are just two weeks away from getting their hands on the latest edition, which has taken almost a decade to make and has become the most expensive title in history. The franchise allows players to act out gangster fantasies — shooting up bars, crashing cars — in fictional renderings of US cities where the soundtrack piped through in-game radio is almost as important as the cutting-edge visuals. GTA VI, which comes 13 years after its predecessor, is expected to break sales records when it lands on November 19 thanks in part to a monumental marketing campaign that kicked off in late 2023 with the first official trailer. “It is going to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time,” Chris Dring of The Game Business outlet told AFP. The previous edition, GTA V, is still the second-biggest selling game ever — it took just three days to rack up $1 billion in sales, two days less than the movie “Avengers: Endgame”. nigeria.title: FCCPC seals firms as oil, salt samples fail fortification tests
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has sealed manufacturing facilities of defaulting food companies after laboratory tests revealed that 12 per cent of vegetable oil and two per cent of salt samples sold in Nigerian markets failed to meet mandatory micronutrient fortification standards. Executive Vice Chairman of FCCPC, Tunji Bello, disclosed this yesterday while presenting findings from a two-month market survey conducted in partnership with the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), which exposed gaps in compliance with Nigeria’s food fortification policy, raising concerns over consumers’ access to essential nutrients through everyday food products. The survey examined 200 randomly selected samples, comprising 100 vegetable oil and 100 salt products collected from households and open markets across Northern and Southern Nigeria. Laboratory analysis revealed that 12 per cent of vegetable oil samples and two per cent of salt samples were inadequately fortified with essential micronutrients at household level. Of the 100 vegetable oil samples, 49 were unbranded, while 51 were branded products. The investigation also uncovered poor adoption of digital traceability systems for monitoring fortified food products along the supply chain. Only six vegetable oil manufacturers had registered on GAIN’s Digital Fortification Quality Traceability Plus platform, while three companies uploaded a combined eight product test results. Bello said large-scale food fortification was a mandatory public health policy aimed at tackling micronutrient deficiencies through the addition of essential nutrients, including vitamin A, iron, folic acid, zinc and iodine. He stated: “Consumers must be able to trust the quality of the products they buy and the health benefits those products are advertised to provide. “Consumer protection goes beyond resolving everyday complaints or halting deceptive business practices. It fundamentally comes down to ensuring that citizens are not denied the essential value, safety and nutritional benefits they pay for in the marketplace.” He said compliance directives had been issued to defaulting manufacturers, stressing that every batch of food products must meet established quality and safety standards. Bello added that the survey findings had been forwarded to the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) for further regulatory action under the existing memorandum of understanding between both agencies. nigeria.title: Trump blames Democrats’ midterm wins for US stock market plunge
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump has blamed the stock market’s sharp decline on the electoral victories recorded by the opposition Democratic Party in the midterm elections earlier this week. Trump made the accusation on Thursday in a post on his Truth Social platform, following a sharp selloff in US equities. “The Stock Market crashed today because the Dumocrats had a big Tuesday — So sad to see, you only have yourselves to blame!” he wrote. However, market analysts attributed the selloff largely to concerns that Democratic electoral gains could threaten investments in artificial intelligence (AI) data centres, amid growing opposition to such projects across the United States. The technology-focused Nasdaq recorded its worst percentage decline in a single session since April 2025. Data centre projects have faced opposition from voters across party lines, with several candidates who won seats in the midterm elections pledging to restrict or slow down their development. The Democrats made significant gains, flipping seats previously held by Republicans in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine. In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins, securing the party’s seventh Senate seat captured from Republicans. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the traditionally conservative state since 1932, while Iowa elected a Democratic senator for the first time since 2008. In Texas, Democrat Talarico declared that he had defeated “Goliath” after winning a Senate seat, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the governorship. Democrats also retained key Senate seats, including that of Jon Ossoff in Georgia, as well as an open seat in New Hampshire. Their gains extended to Michigan, where Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. In the House of Representatives, Democrats recorded gains across Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had won comfortably in 2024. In one closely watched contest in Indiana, Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican Congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump had carried by 17 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. The Democrats also won Georgia’s governorship, with former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms making history as the state’s first Black woman governor. Republicans, however, secured victories in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds became the state’s first Black governor, while Ashley Moody retained a Senate seat after overcoming a strong Democratic challenge. nigeria.description: By Udeme Akpan, Obas Esiedesa & Ediri Ejor There are indications that electricity supply to consumers nationwide has worsened, with Distribution Companies (DisCos) receiving 2,926 megawatts (MW), amid inadequate gas supply, reduced water inflows into hydroelectric reservoirs and other operational constraints. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed a distribution across the DisCos with Abuja, Benin, Eko, Enugu and Ibadan DisCos receiving 633MW, 264MW, 256MW, 253MW and 391MW, respectively. Similarly, Ikeja, Jos, Kaduna, Kano, Port Harcourt and Yola DisCos received 249MW, 146MW, 167MW, 173MW, 320MW and 74MW, respectively. Explaining the decline, NISO stated: “The limited availability of gas has constrained the capacity of affected thermal generating stations to operate at their available levels, while reduced water inflows into reservoirs have impacted the generation capacity of hydroelectric power stations.” The operator added that the constraints had reduced electricity allocations to DisCos, resulting in fewer hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. “Consequently, the reduction in available generation has affected the quantum of electricity allocated to Distribution Companies (DisCos) for onward supply to consumers, thereby resulting in reduced hours of electricity supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks,” it stated further. Similarly, the Federal Ministry of Power acknowledged the impact of the outages on households, businesses and public institutions, particularly in areas that had recently recorded improvements in electricity supply. A statement signed by Adeola Adelabu, Special Adviser (Media and Publicity) to the Minister of Power, the ministry said: “We recognise what every hour without power means for individuals, families and businesses, and we do not take it lightly.” The Ministry further said preliminary assessments showed that the disruptions were not caused by any major or systemic failure of the national grid. It explained: “They stem from maintenance and operational issues on parts of the power ecosystem, together with a decline in generation caused by constraints in gas supply to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower water inflows into reservoirs.” The ministry disclosed that the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, was working with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), NISO and DisCos to resolve the operational constraints, accelerate ongoing maintenance and restore normal supply. nigeria.title: Atiku Takes Presidential Campaign To Kebbi, Pledges To Restore Fuel Subsidy

I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.description: U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth delivering remarks at the event hosted at the Consul General’s residence in Lagos. Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. entertainment.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury
entertainment.description: Ejiro Amos Tafiri , a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work. entertainment.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. sports.description: Billy Sharp has come out of retirement to play for AFC Rushden & Diamonds - and is seeking a landmark goal [BBC] The notion of your football club ceasing to exist is unthinkable for many fans, but for supporters of Rushden & Diamonds it became a sad reality in 2011. The Northamptonshire-based side, backed by the late Max Griggs, rocketed through non-league in the 1990s and in 2003 reached the third tier of English football before financial issues after he stepped away ultimately saw them fold. A community lost its focal point, and within years their Nene Park stadium had been razed to the ground. "It was heartbreaking - we knew we'd been robbed." reflected Rob Usher, the chairman of phoenix side AFC Rushden & Diamonds, who will make their FA Cup first-round debut this weekend. "I think it was that anger that probably fuelled the fans saying 'no, we don't accept it. We're not gone, we're not done and we want our club back." 'This is community' Some 2,000 travelling fans will make their way to see the now eighth-tier Diamonds take on League One side Burton Albion on Saturday - a bittersweet reminder of days the supporters of the original club could have once taken for granted. Usher, like many of those involved with the Northern Premier League Division One Midlands side, has followed both incarnations of the club - firstly as a fan, but also as a groundsman and turnstile operator before becoming chairman in 2022. "My first game was an FA Cup tie against Shrewsbury Town in 1998. It was the year we ended up playing Leeds United in the third round." he said. "Rushden & Diamonds gave us some great times. Winning leagues, the Duane Darby's, the Onandi Lowe's of our past. But I tell everyone I've never traded for what we have with AFC Rushden & Diamonds. "This is a community, this is an army of people who turn up and give their time and their money, their care, their devotion... not because they want the club to exist, but because they want the club to thrive. The 2026 college football season began with expectations that it might preview one of the strongest NFL quarterback classes in recent memory. Instead, the perceived top prospects have been all over the map. Arch Manning and Dante Moore have slid, while Drew Mestemaker has surged and CJ Carr has held steady. sports.description: Virgil van Dijk admits Liverpool's defensive struggles are 'not sustainable' Virgil van Dijk has warned that Liverpool 's defensive record is 'not sustainable' after Fenerbahce scored three times from set-pieces to beat the Reds 3-2 in Istanbul. Andoni Iraola's side led twice in the Champions League on Wednesday, through Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak, but were pegged back quickly on both occasions before Vedat Muriqi headed a 79th-minute winner. The defeat ended Liverpool's perfect record in this season's league phase, but the worry runs deeper than one result. The Reds had also let in three goals in their wins over Villarreal and LASK, the first time Liverpool have ever conceded three or more in three consecutive major European games. It also means back-to-back defeats for the first time under Iraola, following the loss to Arsenal at the weekend. Liverpool's league record makes for better reading, with only three teams having conceded fewer than their nine goals. However, Van Dijk warned his team that their concession of soft goals cannot continue in Europe. "It's definitely not sustainable. That's why it's a very disappointing night for many reasons, but definitely because of the goals we conceded and the manner we conceded them as well. There is work to do." - Virgil van Dijk The captain singled out the set-piece goals as the most frustrating part of the night. "Three set-pieces as well. We have been very good at them so far this season, but we switched off and weren't ready for the first and second balls. It's a tough one to take," he said. Liverpool face Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, the last game before the international break. They sit fifth with 15 points from nine games. Van Dijk said the clash with the Eagles is 'massive' after successive setbacks for Iraola's side. "It's massive. When we are back in Liverpool, preparing and recovering physically and mentally, we will be looking forward. It is always tough at Palace and I don't expect anything different." 'We cannot lose in the manner we did' The Dutchman believes the setbacks can still strengthen the squad. "I mentioned after the last game [against Arsenal] that we as a group have to go through good moments but also lesser good moments," he said. "That will only form a bigger bond and it will be only beneficial. No-one wants to lose games, especially how we did, but it should only help us in the near future. We should not accept losing, especially in the manner we did."

sports.title: Steele dominates Clemens to cap unblemished District 27-6A championship
sports.description: Steele junior Pike Kempe celebrates a win between Steele and Clemens at Lehnhoff Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in Schertz. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) Led by its stingy defense, Steele wrapped up a dominant run through District 27-6A with a 42-14 victory over Clemens on Thursday at Lehnhoff Stadium. Steele (8-1-1, 7-0) racked up 508 yards of total offense, while holding Clemens (7-3, 4-3) to 184 total yards, as the Knights defeated their rivals for the seventh straight time. The Knights came into the game having already clinched their seventh straight district title, but Steele didn't rest on its laurels as it outscored Clemens 35-14 after the game was tied 7-7 early in the second quarter. Steele coach David Saenz said winning the district title for the seventh year in a row was a big accomplishment for the senior class, a group which hasn't lost a district game in four years. "We always talk about protecting the tradition," Saenz said. "It feels good and extremely proud, especially for our seniors to go the four years that they were here without losing a district game and then continuing that tradition of winning a district championship." Steele senior Marshall Kenner rushes into the end zone during a game between Steele and Clemens at Lehnhoff Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in Schertz. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) With the win, Steele leads the all-time series against Clemens 16-2, with the Buffaloes last win against the Knights in 2019. Next up, Steele hosts Reagan (6-3, 6-1) in the bi-district round of the Class 6A Division I playoffs next Thursday at Lehnhoff Stadium. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. Clemens needed a win to clinch a playoff berth. Now the Buffaloes' playoff hopes hinge on the longshot chance that winless San Marcos (0-9, 0-6) can beat East Central (5-4, 3-3) Friday in the regular season finale at 7:30 p.m. at Hornet Stadium. An East Central loss would secure Clemens' first playoff berth in seven years. A Hornets win would result in a tiebreaker, but with Pieper and Judson now both a half-game up on Clemens going into Friday, it could be up to a four-team tie for the final three spots, depending on how Pieper and Judson fare in their matchups against Wagner and New Braunfels Canyon, respectively. The Hornets hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Buffaloes if it comes down to a two-way tie. Clemens coach Alan Hill said his team accomplished a lot in his third season as the Buffaloes' coach, as Clemens produced its first winning season in seven years. "It was really good," Hill said. sports.title: Marcus Rashford reveals what he told Lamine Yamal before leaving Barcelona
sports.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - APRIL 11: Marcus Rashford of FC Barcelona celebrates after scoring his team's fourth goal with his teammate Lamine Yamal during the LaLiga EA Sports match between FC Barcelona and RCD Espanyol de Barcelona at Spotify Camp Nou on April 11, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) | Getty Images Marcus Rashford has spoken admiringly about Lamine Yamal and revealed how he was in touch with his former team-mate about the recent Ballon d’Or awards. The England international has returned to Manchester United after a season with Barcelona , where he won La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup, but says he’s never played with anyone as talented as Yamal. “I talked to Lamine, not after the awards but before. And before I left Barcelona, I told him I’ve played with some talented, talented players, but he’s above them all,” he said, per the Manchester Evening News. “I’ve never seen a player at that age be as talented as what he is. So for me, I’ve never said this out to the media before, but for me, he’s the closest somebody can get to the level of Messi over the years. “It’s only my opinion, but I believe in this guy’s talent so much. So I texted him and just let him know, listen, he’s what, he has finished second, third, and third. “So he’s finished second place, third place, and eighth place so far. And at the age of what, 19? So we’ll see what he does, but if he goes on to win seven Ballons d’Or, I wouldn’t be surprised.” Yamal has gone on to enjoy an impressive start to the season with Barcelona, but it’s been a different story for Rashford. He’s part of a struggling Manchester United squad and is currently sidelined with a hip injury.

Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors have flipped the script on their season, and the superstar guard revealed that a message from head coach Steve Kerr after an 0-3 start helped spark the turnaround. Speaking after Thursday’s 120-100 win over the Miami Heat , which extended Golden State’s winning streak to six games, Curry looked back at what Kerr told the team after a loss to the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 24. “It was in Phoenix, I think he was talking about after that game, I know a lot of guys didn’t play, but he just mentioned sticking with the process and the things that he’d noticed on film and just the feel in games, like we were really close to being able to put together, you know, winning performances,” Curry said after the game. In the latest victory, Curry scored 29 points in just 28 minutes, while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg added 17 points, eight rebounds, six assists and three steals. Nine Warriors finished with at least eight points, a sign of the depth Kerr has been able to lean on. The Warriors, now 6-3, will look to keep the momentum going when they host the Orlando Magic on Saturday before closing their homestand against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. sports.title: Former Australia star Chris Lynn serves one-month ban after testing positive for cocaine on T20 Blast finals day
sports.description: Northamptonshire Steelbacks batter Chris Lynn was handed, and served, a one month ban following a positive drug test for cocaine after the club won the T20 Vitality Blast final on July 18th. The Cricket Regulator confirmed that Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) following a drug test taken on Finals Day and an investigation was launched. Lynn’s urine sample was sent to the WADA -accredited Laboratory in the Laboratoire Anti-Dopage, France for analysis and returned Adverse Analytical Findings (“AAF”) for cocaine’s Metabolite benzoylecgonine meaning that it was a violation of cricket’s anti-doping rule. Cocaine is a substance banned “In Competition” but the investigation found that Lynn had taken the drug on the night of July 15th into the early hours of July 16th outside of competition. Northamptonshire won their Blast quarter-final against Gloucestershire that evening. Having also provided evidence supporting this position the regulator accepted that Lynn’s use of cocaine amounted to an out-of-competition ADR violation and was unrelated to sporting performance. The regulator charged Lynn with two ADR violations in September and sought a suspension of three months. The second of those violations – ADR Article 2.2 – in that the Cricketer Used a Prohibited Substance, namely cocaine, on or before 18 July 2026 (the “ADRVs”) – was withdrawn as the reported level of cocaine in the sample was below the minimum reporting level required. Lynn acknowledged and accepted the findings of the regulator and informed them of his decision to undergo a substance of abuse treatment programme. In October, the regulator received evidence that Lynn had completed the programme and his suspension was reduced to one month. That ban was served between Lynn’s provisional suspension on 31 July 2026 until 11.59pm on 30 August 2026. Northants beat Hampshire in the Vitality Blast T20 final at Edgbaston this year (PA) The findings also concluded that there was no requirement to inflict any sanction Northamptonshire Steelbacks. A statement from the Cricket Regulator reads: “The Cricket Regulator has imposed a one-month suspension on former Northamptonshire Steelbacks cricketer Chris Lynn. The period of suspension has now been served. “Mr Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) for the presence of cocaine's Metabolite, benzoylecgonine, related to an In Competition sample collected on the 18 July 2026. “Mr Lynn has accepted the sanction. No further comment will be made on this matter.”

sports.title: Legendary Real Madrid forward sends message of support to Vinicius amid growing pressure
sports.description: Legendary Real Madrid forward sends message of support to Vinicius amid growing pressure Vinicius Jr. has received public support from legendary Real Madrid teammate Karim Benzema in the wake of his struggle for consistency, growing criticism from fans, and increased competition for his place in the starting XI. Benzema shared a photograph of the two players together on Instagram, prompting Vinicius to repost the message on his own account. The gesture comes at a difficult moment for the 26-year-old, whose performances have attracted considerable scrutiny . Although Jose Mourinho and the club hierarchy continue to back him, his recent absence has coincided with an impressive run of results, while Yan Diomande has emerged as a serious competitor for his preferred position on the left wing. Benzema reminds Vinicius of the support he still has at Real Madrid Benzema’s message is quite significant for the Brazilian given the relationship the two forwards developed during their time together at Real Madrid. Benzema has sent a message of support to Vinicius. (Source: Instagram) The Frenchman and Brazilian formed an effective attacking partnership, with Benzema often helping Vinicius develop his game during his early years in the first team. His Instagram message, which read, “N1 always”, appears to be an expression of confidence in his former teammate at a time when the Brazilian is facing considerable criticism. Vinicius acknowledged the gesture by sharing Benzema’s photograph and message on his own Instagram account. Diomande makes the most of Vinicius’ absence The challenge Vinicius is facing at Real Madrid is no longer limited to the fans, as his four-match LaLiga suspension has provided other players with opportunities to establish themselves. Crucially, Real Madrid have won all three league matches played during his domestic suspension, beating Sevilla 4-1, Barcelona 2-1 and Racing Santander 3-0. Vinicius is going through a tough run of form. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) Quite particularly, Diomande has been particularly impressive , registering four goals and three assists across his last six appearances. Mourinho still has a decision to make over Vinicius Despite the team’s encouraging results, Mourinho has continued to defend Vinicius publicly, as he did so after a 3-2 win over AEK Athens . The Portuguese manager previously emphasised his respect for the Brazilian despite acknowledging that he was not performing at his highest level. However, the forward will now have to demonstrate that he can rediscover his influence in an attacking structure that has functioned effectively without him in recent league matches.

sports.description: William Saliba Arsenal 2026-27 pre-match - Getty William Gallas believes Arsenal defender William Saliba would find it incredibly difficult to turn down a transfer to Real Madrid. The former France international claims the Spanish giants operate on a completely different level to the Gunners despite Mikel Arteta's recent success. Saliba backed for Madrid move Gallas believes Saliba could be tempted to leave Arsenal if Madrid attempt to secure his signature. The French defender has established himself as one of the finest centre-backs in world football since moving to north London. Saliba formed a formidable partnership with Gabriel Magalhaes at the heart of the Arsenal defence. His dominant performances were crucial as Mikel Arteta's side secured the Premier League title last season. The defender committed his long-term future to Arsenal by signing a new contract until 2030 earlier this year. However, Gallas feels the historic allure of a move to the Spanish capital would be too strong to ignore. Real Madrid on a different level Gallas is adamant that the prestige of playing at the Santiago Bernabeu outweighs the Gunners' recent progress. He insists the immense pressure and relentless expectations in Spain set Madrid apart from their European rivals. "Are Arsenal at a high enough level now that William Saliba would turn down Real Madrid if they came in for him?’ Gallas told SeatPick . "I know a lot of people will be mad about what I’m going to say right now but if we are talking about the history of both clubs, Real Madrid and Arsenal, then Real Madrid is Real Madrid. They are on a different level. "For me, even if their performances at the moment are not the best, and even if they haven’t won the biggest trophies recently, Madrid is Madrid, and I’m telling you, any player who has the opportunity to go to Madrid, they will try to go there, and you can’t blame them. You couldn’t blame a player like Saliba if that is his decision." He believes the north London club are simply writing a new chapter rather than dominating an era. "Arsenal and Manchester United?" Gallas added. sports.title: Marcus Rashford says Lamine Yamal is the closest player to Lionel Messi: ‘It won’t surprise me if he wins seven Ballon d’Ors’
sports.description: Marcus Rashford says Lamine Yamal is the closest player to Lionel Messi: ‘It won’t surprise me if he wins seven Ballon d’Ors’ Marcus Rashford has delivered extraordinary praise for Lamine Yamal, describing the Barcelona teenager as the most talented player he has encountered and suggesting he could eventually win seven Ballon d’Or awards. The current Manchester United forward, who had a productive loan spell with Barcelona last season, made the comments during a meeting with supporters at Old Trafford. Notably, Barcelona had an option to permanently buy Rashford, but the Catalan club decided to sign Anthony Gordon instead . Rashford believes Lamine Yamal can match Messi The former Barcelona forward did not hold back when discussing his former teammate, explaining that he had already recognised Yamal’s extraordinary ability before leaving the Catalan club. “Before I left Barça, I told Lamine Yamal that I’d played with some very talented players, but that he’s head and shoulders above them all.” He continued by highlighting the teenager’s exceptional qualities, saying, Rashford has reflected on the talent of Lamine Yamal. (Photo by Judit Cartiel/Getty Images) “I’ve never seen a player of that age with as much talent as him; he’s the closest anyone has come to Messi’s level over the years.” The English forward also backed Yamal’s chances of achieving remarkable individual success, adding, “I really believe in his talent; if he goes on to win seven Ballon d’Ors, it won’t surprise me. He’s finished second, third and eighth. And at what age? Nineteen?” Rashford insists Messi is in a league of his own Despite comparing Yamal’s potential with Messi’s level, Rashford made it clear that he considers the Argentine’s overall footballing ability virtually impossible to replicate. “He’s an incredible player. We’ll probably never see another player in our lifetime who is as complete a genius as Leo.” Rashford has nothing but praise for Messi. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Rashford also discussed the latest Ballon d’Or outcome, where Yamal was one of the favourites, backing Harry Kane as a deserving winner because of his contribution in front of goal and creativity. “He scored an absurd number of goals this year and provided an absurd number of assists. I sent him a text the other day and told him he deserved it.” Rashford explains his Barcelona move The conversation also touched on Rashford’s career decisions and his eventual return to Manchester United following his loan spell at Barcelona. Reflecting on his subsequent experience at Aston Villa, the club where he played before moving to Barcelona, he explained why he did not want to join another English club if a return to Old Trafford was not possible. “I realised one thing… I couldn’t keep playing against United every season. If United isn’t an option, I told my agent to take me abroad – don’t take me to another Premier League club,” he concluded. Source: Mundo Deportivo

technology.title: Safari's Autofill feature may be distorting time
technology.description: The autofill feature of Apple's Safari browser appears to be suffering from a date handling error that occasionally leads it to supply an incorrect credit card expiration date when filling out forms. The supposed issue has been a sore spot for Apple customers dating back at least to 2017, when the author of an Apple Community forum post complained about changes to the month field in the Autofill credit card expiration date when moving between time zones. "I've noticed for the last year or so, whenever I travel from Eastern time zone (my home) to Central time zone or even Pacific time zone that my credit card expiration date month changes in Safari Autofill," the Safari user wrote. Another post in 2021 raised similar concerns. "I don't know how to reproduce this," the author wrote. "Every few months Safari on any of my devices changes the expiration month of all of my stored credit cards by decreasing the month by 1, for example instead of 10/2029 it changes it to 09/2029." Three years later, another person posting to Apple's Community forum reported the same issue. "For a few years now every time I use Autofill on my computer my credit cards (ALL of them) always have their expiration dates change one month earlier," the 2024 post says. "I thought it was just a glitch on my computer but I bought a new computer and didn't transfer anything from my old one and it is still doing it." An unrelated Autofill bug report from 2024 suggests that if there is an issue, it resides in Apple-owned Safari code rather than Safari's open source WebKit engine. Wherever the bug may reside, Safari's unreliable handling of credit card dates has kept a complaint-filled Reddit thread going for four years. And the reported month-shifting has been noted in other threads, too. The Register was unable to reproduce the described behavior, but a reader insists it's still a problem. "The Safari AutoFill feature sometimes fills in the credit card expiration date wrong," the reader explained. "My credit card expires in December, but sometimes Apple helpfully enters November." "To be clear, the card is stored correctly when inspected in Settings," our tipster added. "The off-by-one error only happens when filling out a form in Safari, and not consistently." One possible way this might happen is if the Safari Autofill code implemented the expiration date using Swift's DateComponent type and stored it as a Calendar object with UTC as the TimeZone identifier. So 9/1/2027 at 00:00 would appear as 8/31/2027 at 16:00. Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but we're told Apple's Help Desk – or "Helpless Desk" as our source put it – advised clearing the browser cache and re-entering details of the affected credit card. technology.title: Hospital gave very sick doctor a special PC for his personal, erm, pleasure
technology.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to a fresh edition of On Call, The Register 's weekly tale of tech support trials and tribulations that readers kindly share. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Mason," who told us he once worked at a hospital doing tech support for its research labs. "One of the labs was for a doctor who was one of the world's top organ transplant researchers" Mason told On Call. The doctor was also a voracious consumer of – ahem – adult entertainment, a habit that saw his PC and other machines around the lab often come down with a nasty case of malware. Mason got to clean that up, sometimes multiple times in a single week. The doctor's foibles were widely known around the hospital, as was the fact that his activities violated several workplace policies. Mason pointed this out to his boss every time he cleaned up a fresh malware outbreak but such was the doctor's status that management never intervened. And then the hospital was hit by a nasty cyber-worm that did a lot of damage. During the cleanup, Mason's colleagues found logs that showed the doctor's PC was the source of the infection, and that he had been indulging in his online hobby at the time the worm arrived. Mason assumed this would be the moment at which the doctor would finally be held accountable and face disciplinary action. Instead the doctor made a bargain with the IT department to henceforth use only a designated PC when pursuing – ahem – personal and/or intimate matters. And he would only use office PCs for actual work. The hospital's tech team rescued a PC from its e-waste pile for this job. "Get this thing going and deliver it to Doctor Pervert," Mason's boss ordered. By this stage, Mason had had enough. He escalated his protests, telling his boss that indulging this doctor was unprofessional, likely exposed the hospital to lawsuits, wasted IT department resources, and was just wrong. "What do you want to hear?" his boss replied. "The CIO told me do this or get another job." After Mason prepped that PC, he only needed to clean up malware about once a year – after the poor machine was so overrun with malware that it no longer served the doctor's purposes. Mason left the hospital while this PC was still in place. "You'll be shocked, no doubt, to learn that years later the doctor's graduate students filed a lawsuit," he told On Call. "And that the separate fun-time computer was one of the pieces of evidence that the hospital knew about his – ahem – proclivities and not just ignored them but facilitated them." Have you been asked to cover up revolting behavior? Or ignore policy? Click here to share your story with On Call. It's our policy to tell a great tech support story week, so we appreciate every contribution. ®
